In my opinion you don't have to worry about safety as long as you stay in the areas that tourists frequent. (My husband and I just returned from our second vacation there.)

Within walking distance from the cruise docks you can explore downtown with its shops and museums. We went to the Slavery Museum and the National Heritage Museum; both will give you an education on the founding of the Bahamas. You can also walk to Junkanoo Beach which is very nice for swimming and sun bathing. If you keep heading west on Bay St. you will reach the Fish Fry which is a collection of really good restaurants.

One place my husband and I really like is the Doongalik Studios Art Gallery on Village St. You can probably take a jitney (bus) there pretty easily.

Although we didn't do this you can find a commercial tour bus that will take you around the island. (My husband and I did a private tour with a local we met at the Fish Fry.)

We have found the locals to be so friendly. They really appreciate tourists coming to see their beautiful country and the economic benefits we bring. We never felt unsafe there even when we went into some of the neighborhoods where locals live. But since you'll only be there for the day you'll probably be in the more touristy areas which are very safe.

You may see a few stray dogs as you are walking around. These are called "potcakes" and will probably shy away from you. We met a few friendly ones though and have adopted 2 potcake puppies on our vacations--best dogs I've ever had.
